A lot of people like parroting it whenever they see a green frog or a sad guy or just anything with two p and two e. but the concept behind the meme is deep and it rings back to nearly a decade when rage comics were still all the rage and troll face was used sincerely to troll and not as a "LEL I TRUL U" sarcasm. (this phenomenon is in and of itself incredibly interesting btw) But anyway. The rare pepe refers to the obscure knowledge and the amount of people who can accurately tell you why a meme is funny and what it does when you laugh at it. Most communities no matter the size have memes. A personal joke that you share with your friends is a meme and a deeply valuable and rare one since only you and they can laugh and understand the meaning behind it. Pepe, as well as any other 4chan meme, started on 4chan (obviously) inside most likely one of the bigger boards like /v/, /b/ or /fit/ (which is exceptionally memish because a lot of the users post on reddit and tumblr too) outside of these three boards memes tend to live their lives and die quietly when the users no longer have a need for them or when they run their natural course. 4channers are particularly wary and weary of memes that overstay their welcome precisely because they understand that it works a link between reddit and 4chan when you recognize and post because of that meme. If they keep posting the same meme and it becomes popular then it also turns into a breadcrumb trail leading straight to them where any newfag can come and shit up the site with their retarded etiquette and political correctness. So instead 4channers make the memes, laugh for a while, and then violently disconnect themselves from it and mock anyone who mentions it as being retarded and cancerous precisely because they act similarly to a cancer would, spreading and refusing to die unless directly attacked and destroyed. But at the same time 4channers still love memes (and don't let them tell you any different. 4chan is the center of memes and memetic behavior even if they do have to kill it once it becomes popular) and they want to keep enjoying them even after they've run their course. "rare pepe" personifies this nostalgia towards lost memes by directly saying that a meme can only be valuable when nobody knows it exists outside of the select group who made it. A rare pepe that is shared is similar to a rage comic that reaches facebook and has your grandma posting advice animals while at the same time using them wrong. It's a strange irony that people use it without realizing what it memes, when the meme itself is mocking those who use memes without personally understanding them or having any connection to them outside of seeing them posted on a reddit thread and parroting it elsewhere because it will be funny. Memes were meant to die, because a meme can only be funny when a certain group of people use it. Once it's out there and in the spotlight a meme is no longer funny to the core group. It just becomes some sort of macabre puppet that vaguely resembles what you once thought was hilarious. For a related meme, please look at REEEEEE NORMIES GET OFF MY BOARD!!! which in a similar vein represents the frustration of someone who sees their favorite jokes mangled by those who want to use it without understanding it.

It says he usually traveled with bodyguards, but his bodyguards weren't with him because they couldn't get tickets for the same flight. He was found dead the next day in his hotel bed by a cleaner who found the door locked from the inside and then had it opened by security.

12 of whom carried British passports, six Irish, four French, one German, and four Australian, and another two Palestinians who were arrested. Those citizens apparently had no idea that their identities were being used and the UK even launched an investigation into it.

Without re-writing the Wiki article, this is what happened:

When al-Mabhouh arrived around 3 p.m., two of the suspects who were dressed in tennis attire followed him to determine which room he had checked into (which is No. 230), as well as the number of the room immediately across the hall (No. 237). The information is alleged by the Dubai police to have been communicated to a third party, who then telephoned from a different hotel to book room 237. According to surveillance videos, the individual who checked into 237 did not enter the room, but appears to have given the room key to an accomplice in the lobby of the hotel, and immediately have left Dubai, prior to the assassination. Al-Mabhouh, later, left the hotel and while several of the suspects kept watching, it is thought that (a) suspect(s) tried to gain entry to his room. One of the lookout suspects could be seen on video delaying a tourist who exits the elevator on the second floor at this time, apparently to give other team members time to act. The evidence for this is the fact that four men arrived by elevator and entered the hallway where the victim's room and the alleged perpetrator's rooms were located at this time, and the same four men immediately left after the assassination is supposed to have happened.

Major General Khamis Mattar al-Mazeina as the deputy commander of Dubai's police gave details of the death of al-Mabhouh after forensic tests.
